notes.content:
**India** is a **parliamentary democracy** — supreme power lies with the **people**. The Constitution calls India a **Union of States**; power is divided between the **Centre and the states**.

| Organ | Job | At the Centre |
|---|---|---|
| **Legislature** | **Makes** laws | Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President) |
| **Executive** | **Executes** (enforces) laws | President, Vice President, PM, Council of Ministers |
| **Judiciary** | **Interprets** laws; checks the other two | Supreme Court → High Courts → Subordinate Courts |

**Three Lists** (subjects for law-making)
| Union List (Centre only) | State List (states) | Concurrent List (both) |
|---|---|---|
| Defence, banking, railways, post & telegraph, airways & shipping, foreign affairs | Public health, agriculture, prisons, water supply, markets & fairs, land tenures | Education, electricity, factories & trade unions, forests, population control, cruelty to animals |

In a **conflict** over a Concurrent subject, the **central law prevails**.

notes.subtopic: 2. Lok Sabha — House of the People

fiveW.who: Members directly elected by the people
fiveW.why: To represent the people directly and make laws
fiveW.how: Universal Adult Suffrage (18+) with secret ballot; seats by population

notes.content:
**Composition**
• **Maximum strength 552**: up to **530** from states, up to **20** from Union Territories, **2 Anglo-Indians** nominated by the President (as per textbook; this nomination ended in 2020).
• Seats allotted by **population**; seats **reserved for SCs and STs**.

**Election:** **directly** elected by **Universal Adult Suffrage** — every citizen **18+** can vote regardless of caste, religion or sex; **secret ballot**.

**Qualifications of a member:** Indian citizen · at least **25 years** · sound mind · not bankrupt or convicted.

**Term:** **5 years**; the President can **dissolve** it earlier; can be **extended during an Emergency**.

**Sessions:** summoned by the President; **gap not more than 6 months**; three sessions — **Budget, Monsoon, Winter**.

**Speaker:** elected by Lok Sabha members; presides, regulates debates, keeps discipline.

fiveW.who: Representatives of states and UTs + 12 nominated members
fiveW.when: Permanent house; one-third retire every 2 years
fiveW.why: To represent the states and bring expert experience
fiveW.how: Indirect election by proportional representation (single transferable vote)

notes.content:
• Also called the **Upper House / Council of States**.
• **Presiding officer:** the **Vice President** (ex-officio Chairperson).

**Composition:** **maximum 250** — **238 elected** (states and UTs) + **12 nominated** by the President (special knowledge in **science, arts, literature, social service**). Seats by state population.

**Election:** **indirect**, by **proportional representation** through the **single transferable vote**.

**Qualification:** same as Lok Sabha, but minimum age **30 years**.

**Term:** **permanent house** — never dissolved; **one-third retire every 2 years**; a member serves **6 years**.

| | Lok Sabha | Rajya Sabha |
|---|---|---|
| Max strength | 552 | 250 |
| Election | Direct | Indirect |
| Min age | 25 | 30 |
| Term | 5 years (dissolvable) | Permanent; members 6 years |
| Presiding officer | Speaker | Vice President |

notes.subtopic: 4. How a Bill Becomes a Law
notes.content:
• **Bill** = draft of a proposed law.
• **Ordinary bill** — can start in **either House**. **Money bill** — **only in the Lok Sabha**.

**Three stages**
1. **Introduced** in a House.
2. **Debate and voting**; then sent to the **other House**, which follows the same procedure. (For a **money bill**, the Rajya Sabha gets only **14 days**.)
3. Sent to the **President for assent** — the President may **sign** or **return** it for reconsideration (not a money bill).

Once the President **signs**, the bill becomes an **Act**.

fiveW.who: President (Rashtrapati) — head of the State and first citizen
fiveW.when: Term of 5 years; can be re-elected
fiveW.why: To head the State and act as its constitutional guardian
fiveW.how: Elected indirectly by an electoral college of MPs and MLAs

notes.content:
**Qualifications:** citizen · at least **35 years** · **no office of profit** · qualified to be a Lok Sabha member.

**Election:** **indirectly** by an **electoral college** of **MPs and MLAs**; term **5 years**; can be re-elected.
**Vacancy:** end of term, death, resignation, **impeachment** (for violating the Constitution, treason or corruption — by Parliament).

**Powers**
• **Executive:** appoints the **PM** (leader of majority/coalition) and ministers on the PM's advice; appoints Attorney General, CAG, Governors, ambassadors, Chief Election Commissioner, UPSC members, **Supreme Court and High Court judges**.
• **Military:** **Supreme Commander** of the Defence Forces; declares war and peace.
• **Legislative:** summons Parliament, **dissolves the Lok Sabha**, assents to bills, nominates members, issues **ordinances** (temporary laws when Parliament is not in session; lapse **6 weeks** after it reassembles).
• **Financial:** budget presented in his/her name; money bills need consent; controls the **Contingency Fund**.
• **Judicial:** **pardons** or reduces sentences, even death sentences.
• **Emergency:** **National** (war/external aggression/armed rebellion), **President's Rule** in a state, **Financial** — with Parliament's approval.
• **Discretionary:** if no party has a majority, chooses a PM who can command one.

• Elected **indirectly** by an electoral college of **members of both Houses of Parliament only**; term **5 years**.
• Removed by a resolution of the **Rajya Sabha** passed by a majority, agreed to by the **Lok Sabha**.
• **Acts as President** if the President resigns, dies in office, or is unable to act due to illness/absence.

**Functions:** **ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha** — regulates debates and proceedings; decides admissibility of questions and resolutions; heads committees.

notes.subtopic: 7. Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

fiveW.who: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
fiveW.when: Usually 5 years; earlier if a no-confidence motion passes
fiveW.what: Real executive — head of the government
fiveW.why: The President is only the nominal head; the PM runs the government
fiveW.how: President appoints the leader of the Lok Sabha majority as PM; other ministers on the PM's advice

notes.content:
• **President = nominal/constitutional head of the State; PM = head of the government** — the **pivot** of the constitutional machinery.
• **Appointment:** the President must appoint the **leader of the majority party** in the Lok Sabha; if no majority, parties join to form a **coalition government**.
• **Term:** usually 5 years; ends earlier if a **no-confidence motion** is passed.

**Three categories of ministers:** **Cabinet Ministers** (inner core — finance, railways, defence, home, foreign affairs) · **Ministers of State** · **Deputy Ministers** (the latter two do not attend Cabinet meetings).

**Functions of the PM and Cabinet**
• **Formulate policies**; run and coordinate administration.
• President makes major appointments on their **advice**.
• PM is the **link between the President and the Cabinet**; **allocates portfolios** (a minister who disagrees must resign).
• **Chief spokesperson** of the government in Parliament.
• Represents India abroad (e.g. **NAM**).

**First PM:** Jawaharlal Nehru.

fiveW.who: Chief Justice + up to 30 other judges (as per textbook)
fiveW.when: Since 1950 (first CJI H.J. Kania, 1950–51); judges serve till 65
fiveW.what: Highest court — guardian of the Constitution
fiveW.why: To interpret the Constitution and protect Fundamental Rights
fiveW.how: Original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction; judicial review; writs

notes.content:
• India has a **single, unified judiciary**; the Supreme Court is the **guardian of the Constitution** — can declare any law **null and void** if unconstitutional.
• **Composition:** **Chief Justice** + maximum **30 other judges** (textbook; now 33).
• **First Chief Justice:** **H.J. Kania** (1950–51).
• **Appointment:** by the **President**, after consulting SC and HC judges.
• **Removal:** **impeachment** by Parliament for proven misbehaviour or incapacity; may resign in writing.
• **Term:** till **65 years**.
• **Qualifications:** citizen; **5 years a High Court judge** OR **10 years an advocate** of a High Court OR a **distinguished jurist**.

**Jurisdiction**
• **Original** (heard first here): Centre vs states; states vs states; **violation of Fundamental Rights** (writs).
• **Appellate:** appeals against High Courts — constitutional, civil, criminal.
• **Advisory:** advises the President (advice not binding).

**Other powers:** **Court of Record** (judgements are **precedents**) · **Revisory** (can review its own judgements) · **Judicial review** (examines laws and orders for constitutionality).

**High Court** — apex court of a **state**; may cover one or more states/UTs; UTs fall under a neighbouring state's High Court; **Delhi has its own**.
• **Composition:** Chief Justice + judges (number **not fixed**).
• **Appointment:** by the **President**, consulting the **CJI** and the state **Governor** (and the HC Chief Justice for other judges).
• **Removal:** by impeachment, like SC judges.
• **Qualifications:** citizen; **10 years judicial office** or **10 years advocate** of a High Court.
• **Term:** till **62 years**.
• **Original jurisdiction:** Fundamental Rights, **election petitions**, wills, marriages, divorces, contempt of court. **Appellate:** appeals from subordinate courts.

**Subordinate courts:** **District Court** and **Sessions Court** — highest in a district.

**Nyaya Panchayats (proposed 2011):** elected village courts for **fair, speedy justice** at people's doorsteps; conciliation first; reservation for women, SCs, STs.

**Writs** — written court orders to enforce **Fundamental Rights**: **habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, certiorari** (issued by SC and HCs).

questions.answer:
• Composition: max 552 — up to 530 from states, 20 from UTs, 2 Anglo-Indians nominated (textbook); seats by population; reserved seats for SCs/STs.

questions.question: How does a bill become a law?
questions.answer:
• First stage: the bill (draft law) is introduced in a House — a money bill only in the Lok Sabha.
  • Second stage: debate and voting; then the same procedure in the other House (Rajya Sabha has only 14 days for a money bill).
  • Third stage: sent to the President, who signs it or returns it for reconsideration; once signed it becomes an Act.

questions.question: How is the President elected?
questions.answer: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of the elected Members of Parliament (MPs) and Members of the Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) of the states, for a term of 5 years; he/she can be re-elected.

questions.question: Describe the powers of the President of India.
questions.answer:
• Executive: appoints the PM, ministers, Governors, judges, Attorney General, CAG, Chief Election Commissioner.
  • Military: Supreme Commander; declares war and peace.
  • Legislative: summons Parliament, dissolves the Lok Sabha, assents to bills, nominates members, issues ordinances.
  • Financial: budget in his/her name; money bills need consent; Contingency Fund.
  • Judicial: pardon or reduce sentences.
  • Emergency: national, state (President's Rule), financial.

questions.question: Why is the President called the nominal head of the State while the PM is the real head?
questions.answer:
• All executive power is exercised in the President's name, but he/she acts on the advice of the PM and Council of Ministers.
  • The President must appoint the leader of the Lok Sabha majority as PM.
  • The PM and Cabinet actually frame policies, run the administration and answer to Parliament — so the PM is the real executive and the President the constitutional/nominal head.

questions.question: State three functions of the Vice President.
questions.answer:
• Ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha — regulates debates and proceedings.
  • Decides the admissibility of questions and resolutions; heads committees.
  • Acts as President if the President dies, resigns or is unable to act.

questions.question: What is the role of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet?
questions.answer:
• Formulate policies and run the administration.
  • President makes major appointments on their advice.
  • PM coordinates departments and is the link between the President and the Cabinet.
  • PM distributes portfolios; a minister in conflict must resign.
  • PM is the chief spokesperson in Parliament and represents India abroad (e.g. NAM).

questions.question: Give any two qualifications of a Supreme Court judge.
questions.answer:
• Must be a citizen of India.
  • Must have been a High Court judge for 5 years, or an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.

questions.question: Distinguish between original and appellate jurisdiction. What is judicial review?
questions.answer:
Original jurisdictionAppellate jurisdiction
Cases heard for the first timeAppeals against lower court judgements
Centre vs states; state vs state; Fundamental RightsConstitutional, civil, criminal cases from High Courts

Judicial review: the Supreme Court's power to examine laws of the legislature and orders of the executive and strike down those against the Constitution — it keeps both within constitutional limits.

questions.question: Why is the Supreme Court called the guardian of the Constitution?
questions.answer:
• It interprets the Constitution — its interpretation is final.
  • Through judicial review it can declare any law or order null and void if it violates the Constitution.
  • It protects Fundamental Rights by issuing writs.

questions.question: What are writs? Name any three.
questions.answer: Writs are written orders issued by the Supreme Court and High Courts to enforce Fundamental Rights — commanding someone to do or not do an act. Examples: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition (also quo warranto, certiorari).

questions.question: What is a High Court? What is its jurisdiction? Do all UTs have a High Court?
questions.answer:
• The highest court in a state; may cover one or more states/UTs.
  • Original: Fundamental Rights, election petitions, wills, marriages, divorces, contempt of court. Appellate: appeals from subordinate courts.
  • No — UTs come under a neighbouring state's High Court; Delhi has its own.
